messages.subject: GUESS for calibrated data
parts:
Hi Christen,

Thanks for directing me to this page and the useful discussion. In response to my earlier query about a using weights=TRUE with the akde function, you suggested that to fix very slow computation times (and occasionally, non completion)  that I calibrate the data and use a smaller value of dt, suggesting 4 minutes. I have done this by working through the vignettes but have run into the following error at line 4 below. Any advice on what is preventing the estimation of GUESS greatly appreciated.

 > GUESS <- ctmm.guess(feralcat, CTMM=ctmm(error=TRUE), interactive=FALSE)

Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "SVF", value = 0) :  replacement has 1 row, data has 0



1.     dt <- c(20,96) %#% "minute"  

2.     #dt <- 4 %#% "minute"  

 

3.     vg.feralcat <- variogram(feralcat, dt=dt, fast=FALSE)  # for calibrated data using uere()

 

4.     GUESS <- ctmm.guess(feralcat, CTMM=ctmm(error=TRUE), interactive=FALSE)  

 

5.     fitted.mods <- ctmm.select(feralcat, CTMM=GUESS, 

level   = 1,

method  = "pHREML", 

control = list(method="pNewton", cores = 2),

trace = TRUE, 

verbose=TRUE) 

 

6.     summary(fitted.mods) 

 

 

David

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: GUESS for calibrated data
parts:
Hi David,

"that this will provide an inaccurate estimate for very eccentric distributions" is with regards to forcing isotropic=TRUE to obtain a bandwidth scalar, rather than a matrix. I will clarify the documentation.

With a grid size for the one individual of 1 second (compared to 21-28 seconds), you should expect optimization to take 21-28 times longer to run as is. There are a few options to remedy this given in the documentation on bandwidth, for exactly when that happens: https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/bandwidth.html

On the other hand, if the data contain some very tiny time intervals, say 1 second among hourly sampled data, then the default dt setting will create an excessively high-resolution discretization of time, which will also cause slowdown. In this case CTMM should contain an error model and dt can likely be increased to a larger fraction of the median sampling interval.


fast=FALSE uses exact times and has a computational cost as low as O(n^2), including O(n^2) function evaluations. With PC="direct" this method will produce a result that is exact to within machine precision, but with a computational cost of O(n^3). fast=FALSE,PC='direct' is often the fastest method with small datasets, where n ≤ O(1,000), but scales terribly with larger datasets.


Best,
Chris
